idiom_name: Jest describe/it with beforeEach hooks and expect matchers
implementation_notes: Jest's describe/it tree supplies the skeleton: beforeEach/afterEach hooks and scoped describe blocks carry the fixture beats, each it body performs one act and then expect(...) matchers - the classic Testcase Class is replaced by the callback tree, and hooks declared inside a describe apply only to that block. The runtime's node:test offers the same shape without a dependency, and several expect calls exploring one outcome are still one behaviour; Mocha/Vitest share the API.
pitfalls: An async it that forgets to return or await its promise passes before the act settles; Jest then reports the failure in a later test, which reads as an unrelated break.
Outer beforeEach hooks run before inner ones and afterEach hooks in reverse order, so a test that re-arranges inside its body hides the real fixture from the reader.
expect(...).toBe compares with Object.is while toEqual is the structural comparison, and an expect(...) call with no matcher counts as a passing test.

variants.name: Cucumber-js Gherkin scenario with Given/When/Then steps
variants.idiom_name: Cucumber-js feature files with step definitions over a World object
variants.implementation_notes: The Given-When-Then formulation as an executable specification: the scenario lives in a .feature file and each step is bound in a step-definition file, with state carried between steps on the World object (this) - the three beats are named by the DSL rather than by comments, and the assertion belongs in the Then step. Choose it when the same scenarios must be readable by non-programmers; keep unit-level loops in Jest/Vitest where the ceremony is lower.
pitfalls: Step definitions are global: two features using the same step text share one implementation, so state leaks through the World object unless a Before hook resets it.
Steps that encode UI mechanics ('I click the third row') turn the feature file into a script and lose the specification value; keep steps at the behaviour level.
Assertions placed in Given steps report as setup failures, so failures stop localising to the Then beat - assert only where the scenario declares an outcome.
